newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean shipments normal at Paranagua-union.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean shipments normal at Paranagua-union.

text.p: Shipments of Brazilian soybeans and soymeal from Paranagua port were unaffected as yet by a dockworkers' dispute over pay, a union official said.
But he added that loading of other commodities including orange juice, cotton and wood had already slowed down.

Dockworkers who are demanding a 21 percent wage increase had scaled down all manual operations, in particular the handling of containers, said Nelson Bandeira, secretary of the Paranagua Unions Council.
"The loading of grains has not been affected because most of it is automated and there is very little manual labour involved," Bandeira said.
Paranagua port authorities earlier said the port was operating normally and traders reported that grain shipments were proceeding at full speed.

But Bandeira said loading of other commodities was being slowed. "These include orange juice, cotton, wood, chicken and cattle," he said. Port authorities were not immediately available to confirm this.
